I farm in Quzhou County on irrigated land, and with 40 years in the field I do not spread myself evenly just for appearance. I will keep wheat and maize as the backbone because they are the most reliable for my land and water conditions, I will keep a moderate area of squash because it fits my current cropping focus and brings cash if managed carefully, and I will keep a smaller millet area because it is hardy and useful for risk balance. Since I have well irrigation, I will push the higher-return crops with better seed and moderate-to-high fertilizer, especially maize, wheat, and squash. I will still control costs by not overwatering millet and by keeping pesticide use tied to pressure rather than spraying blindly. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage for maize, millet, and squash because it is efficient on my scale, while I will plough before wheat to leave a firmer, deeper seedbed. My goal is stable yield first, then income, not chasing the highest possible output with unnecessary input.
